title: Second-Contract Thresholds for Retail Installment Contracts, by Credit Tier
content:
When a borrower who already holds an open contract under Retail Installment Contracts asks to finance a second vehicle, three thresholds apply, and they are always those of the **new** contract's tier.

| New contract's tier | Installments paid on the existing contract, at least | Days past due on the existing contract, at most | Combined principal of all open contracts after booking, at most (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 6 Fresh Start | 12 | 0 | 20000.00 |
| Tier 5 Rebuild | 12 | 0 | 25000.00 |
| Tier 4 Standard | 12 | 0 | 30000.00 |
| Tier 3 Advantage | 9 | 0 | 35000.00 |
| Tier 2 Preferred | 9 | 9 | 40000.00 |
| Tier 1 Select | 6 | 9 | 50000.00 |

The installments paid and days past due are measured on the existing open contract; the combined principal counts every open contract of the borrower after the new contract books.

**Hypothetical comparisons.**

- An existing contract 5 days past due meets the Tier 2 Preferred and Tier 1 Select limit of 9 days but not the limit of 0 days that the other four tiers set.
- With an existing contract carrying 11 installments paid, a new Tier 3 Advantage contract (at least 9) meets the installment threshold, while a new Tier 4 Standard contract (at least 12) does not.
- A borrower whose existing contract has 16400.00 of principal and who seeks a new Tier 5 Rebuild contract of 9100.00 reaches combined principal of 25500.00, above the Tier 5 Rebuild limit of 25000.00.
